capture: Continuous screen recording of actual local browser interactions and two real model API requests. No prediction substitution; the initial 0.05-second page-load interval was trimmed.
presentation: Opt-in /#presentation view. Browser capture resized from 1440x720 to 1920x960 without cropping; original English captions appended in a 120-pixel strip. No audio track.

captions.title: MINI JEV / LIVE LOCAL DEMONSTRATION
captions.text:
Small typed decisions from a frozen language model.
Candidate-token scores become structured values; no answer text is generated.

captions.title: 1 / DEFINE THE ALLOWED ANSWERS
captions.text:
Choice: define support queues and what each candidate means.
The model selects a key; software constructs the typed response.

captions.title: 2 / DEFINE A BINARY QUESTION
captions.text:
Noul: ask whether urgency is explicitly requested.
The output is P(true), normalized over the two candidates.

captions.title: 3 / DEFINE ORDERED STAGES
captions.text:
Score: define ordered, equally spaced priority stages.
The output is their probability-weighted mean, not a class ID.

captions.title: RUN / ACTUAL MODEL INFERENCE
captions.text:
Run three questions on the live model.
Each question is evaluated separately.

captions.title: INSPECT / URGENT BILLING MESSAGE
captions.text:
Read the route, urgency probability, and expected priority together.
Each card also shows the distribution over its allowed candidates.

captions.title: CHANGE THE INPUT / RUN AGAIN
captions.text:
Load a routine account request.
Previous results are marked stale until the next run completes.

captions.title: COMPARE / ROUTINE ACCOUNT MESSAGE
captions.text:
Compare how the route, urgency probability, and priority change.
These values are live model outputs, not prefilled answers.

captions.title: INSPECT / THE ACTUAL REQUEST
captions.text:
The request contains the state, instructions, and candidate meanings.
The same interface is available through the Python SDK and HTTP API.

captions.title: INSPECT / THE ACTUAL RESPONSE
captions.text:
Scroll through the typed answers, probabilities, and calibration metadata.
The full JSON remains available for inspection and export.

captions.title: EXPORT / COPY THE LIVE RESPONSE
captions.text:
Copy the JSON response for use in your own tools.
The confirmation shows whether the clipboard operation succeeded.

captions.title: INTERPRET / KNOW WHAT THE NUMBERS MEAN
captions.text:
Probabilities compare allowed candidates only; concentration is not correctness.
A well-typed output can still be semantically wrong.

captions.title: EVIDENCE / WHAT THE PAPER FOUND
captions.text:
Direct readout and native one-token selection agreed in all 1,350 pairs.
This study did not establish a latency advantage over one-token selection.

captions.text:
github.com/UpHash-Network/mini-jev  •  branch: research/eacl2027-demo
Follow demo/README.md. Tested on Apple Silicon; model weights are separate.

clipboard_verification: The isolated recording browser was granted clipboard permission for the loopback demo. Its freshly copied response was read back and exactly matched the visible live response JSON.
limits: Two English support examples demonstrate software use; they are not a quality benchmark. Live UI timing is separate from the unchanged paper study. Large JSON is shown in sequential scroll positions rather than all fields in one frame.
final_visual_review: Passed for the inspected scenes and boundaries. Parent inspected 15 representative frames from the first revised encode; a second AI reviewer inspected 17 representative scenes and then 24 boundary frames from this final artifact. The final encode uses the same captured footage, adjusts caption timing, and shortens the Run instruction. All 39 required DOM rectangles fit the capture viewport; full-file decoding passed. This is not an every-frame human review or a user comprehension study.
